newsitem.title: USA: Japan says U.S. won't supervise on deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Japan says U.S. won't supervise on deregulation.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, contradicting U.S. officials, said that the United States would not have an advisory or supervisory role on Japan's efforts to deregulate key sectors of its economy.
"It's not an advisory role," Hashimoto said, speaking through an interpreter. "We have no intention of being supervised."
"Deregulation is a task that we have to embark upon for ourselves," Hashimoto said.

"Of course we are friends, so we are ready to discuss matters with the United States in that kind of context," Hashimoto added. "Yesterday we were able to reach an understanding to establish a framework for such a dialogue."
Earlier Thursday, the United States said it would advise Japan as it deregulated key sectors of the Japanese economy under an agreement reached early Thursday, U.S. officials said.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters the agreement would allow U.S. officials to have input in Japan's deregulation though "bilateral consultations" on such areas as telecommunications, financial services and medical equipment.
